overall: The AG found a councilor's January 14, 2011 email to a quorum soliciting support for a ballot question was a Open Meeting Law violation, but found the phone calls were below quorum and the Council's remedial response appropriate; no order issued.

allegations.summary: A councilor emailed all fellow councilors asking whether they supported a term-limits ballot question, allegedly a deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Councilor Cronin's January 14, 2011 email to a quorum of his fellow Council members, requesting that the members report whether or not they support a special election for a ballot question, was a deliberation in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The councilor's follow-up phone calls with three councilors about the agenda were alleged to be a serial deliberation among members.
allegations.key_passage: As the phone conversations, even if serial in nature, were between or among at most four members of the Council—less than a quorum—there is no violation of the Open Meeting Law resulting from these phone calls.

allegations.summary: Whether the Council's response to the complaint (withdrawing the topic, releasing the email, memo to members) adequately cured the violation.
allegations.key_passage: However, we fmd that the Council's actions in response to the complaint filed on January 18, 2011 were appropriate.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
